questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:

options.text: Seeing other drivers' faces.
Watching the trailer in your mirrors.
Feeling the trailer move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Looking at your trailer in your mirrors is the easiest way to see if it is skidding. You can spot skidding early by checking your mirrors regularly.

questions.question: When testing ____, move your vehicle forward slowly and press the brakes with the hand control.

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System
The emergency braking system
The trailer service brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer service brakes
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. The brakes should activate if they are working correctly.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release the air pressure and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.

options.text: Rear service line shut-off valve
Rear supply line shut-off valve
Inner shut-off valves

questions.correctAnswerText: Inner shut-off valves
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, keep all shut-off valves open except the ones at the very back of the trailer. This keeps air flowing to all brakes and prevents air from escaping.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:

options.text: May not couple correctly.
Will couple securely.
Is not an issue.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. If the trailer is too low, the nose may be damaged. If the trailer is too high, it will not couple correctly.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Driving combination vehicles takes more skill. They are longer, heavier, and roll over more easily than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: To help prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Placed as high as possible inside a trailer.
Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
Placed on the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Place cargo as low as possible in a trailer. A top-heavy vehicle is more likely to roll over.

questions.question: If you must cross traffic while driving a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
Rely only on your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Wait for a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: Older trailers without spring brakes will have no brakes if:

options.text: The trailer will stop normally.
The air supply leaks away.
The trailer will speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air supply leaks away.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks, there will be no brakes and the wheels will spin freely.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a rig can:

options.text: Help you drive faster.
Prevent a rollover.
Make turns more dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a rollover.
questions.explanation: Uneven cargo loading causes rollovers. Keep the load centered to prevent a rollover.

questions.question: What color identifies service lines on air brake systems?

options.text: White
Yellow
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue
questions.explanation: Air lines use color codes to help drivers avoid mistakes. Blue marks service lines. Red marks emergency lines.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must always stay closed to keep air in the braking system.

questions.question: When turning a corner, what do the rear wheels do?

options.text: Follow the same path as the front wheels.
Follow a different path than the front wheels.
Should not be a concern to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow a different path than the front wheels.
questions.explanation: Rear wheels follow a different path than front wheels when turning. This is called off-tracking. Longer vehicles have greater off-tracking than shorter vehicles.

questions.question: What is true about driving combination vehicles?

options.text: They are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
They require less skill than single commercial vehicles.
They require more skill than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to what?

options.text: Relay valves.
Trailer air tanks.
Signal line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (supply line) does two things. It supplies air to trailer air tanks and controls emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.
Assume it has ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check for ABS, look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor without a trailer
A tractor attached to two trailers
A tractor with a tank

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Drivers must be careful when operating bobtail tractors.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
A valve that shows the fuel level
A valve that limits cargo weight

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar (also called the trolley valve or trailer hand valve) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: When coupling vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all vehicles are the same.
Make sure you couple correctly.
Accept cracks in the mounting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling can be extremely dangerous.

questions.question: If the trailer spring brakes don't release when you push the air supply control, what should you do?

options.text: Check the air line connections.
Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the air line connections.
questions.explanation: Check that all equipment works before driving. If the trailer spring brakes don't release, make sure the air line connections are attached and sealed properly.
